authorization: Owner requested server-side status synchronization repair so stale client updates cannot undo completed jumps, preserving 5071 and all valid interdictions. This continues the authorized jump/travel repair and deployment work.

policy.managed_ship: Any retained journey or durable travel receipt makes the existing server location authoritative. No expiry or inferred move back to an old destination.
policy.managed_player: Check travel history across all ships linked to that shard player, so a different or new ship GUID cannot overwrite the player location.
policy.stale_report: Keep success-compatible status response, return canonical locations plus location_sync.status=ignored/code=stale_location and ignored_for; emit request-correlated status_location_ignored without credentials.
policy.locks: Persisted ship then old/new players in ascending ID order, retained through status response construction; no journey/receipt locks acquired in status paths.
policy.identity: Managed ship identity/model/shard cannot be reassigned through status to bypass travel protection; entire attempt rolls back.
policy.compatibility: Ships/players with no saved server travel history retain status initialization/external relocation behavior. Wallet updates stay independent. New, nested and legacy status forms covered.
policy.limitation: Unversioned status cannot distinguish stale location from an intentional external relocation after travel. Such locations are preserved and require actual server travel or a separately designed explicit reconciliation mechanism.
policy.paused: Do not realign mismatched players, alter timing, resume, cancel, refund, recreate cargo or touch managed ships for recency.

validation.environment: Dedicated synthetic loopback PostgreSQL18 database star_trader_ac3_jump_diagnostic_test; single test worker; real RabbitMQ disabled; no production test writes.
validation.browser: No browser/UI change; no browser tests run. Chrome-only preference retained.
